clue.text: See 16
Misnamed historical period? "Unfair!" (Times)

parts.note: unfair taken as not fair-skinned or fair-haired, i.e. dark
times or eras can be called ages

explanation.surface: Someone protests that a historical era's label is unjust, citing a newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: '(Times)' looks like a newspaper credit but simply means ages; 'Unfair' is the opposite of fair in the complexion sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Historians now argue the early medieval era was not really benighted, so its popular label is a misnomer.

clue.text: About mating: joke about taking tail off

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the word for a joke is read backwards

parts.note: a pun is a joke on words

indicators.note: off signals the letters of tail are put out of order

explanation.surface: A remark on sex: a joke concerning docking an animal's tail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns PUN into NUP; 'off' shuffles TAIL into TIAL; 'taking' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuptial is an adjective concerning marriage or, in zoology, mating behaviour.

clue.text: It makes some people get fit all of a sudden

definitions.text: It makes some people get fit all of a sudden

parts.words: It makes some people get fit all of a sudden
parts.note: reads like an instant exercise regime, but the fit is a seizure that strikes without warning

explanation.surface: A miracle product that makes people healthy overnight.
explanation.definitionFit: Epilepsy is a neurological condition whose sufferers have sudden seizures, also called fits.

clue.text: In a slurred fashion, regret the passing of a cult US TV series and variety

indicators.note: speaking with a slur blurs the double S into SH, so the phrase is said as if drunk

parts.words: regret the passing of a cult US TV series
parts.note: to miss is to regret losing something, and M*A*S*H was a cult US TV comedy series

explanation.surface: A drunken fan mourns the cancellation of a favourite American show.
explanation.definitionFit: A mishmash is a confused jumble, so a variety or medley of things.

clue.text: Brummie has a — as one might say — short unfinished book: "Circle of the Romantic English Composer"

indicators.note: the setter's own 'I've a' is meant to be heard spoken, which gives a first name

parts.note: Brummie is the setter, so 'Brummie has a' is 'I've a', sounding like a forename

indicators.note: unfinished removes the final letter of the word for the book

parts.note: a novella is a short novel, which 'short' points to
a circle is the shape of the letter O

explanation.surface: The setter claims to own a fragment of a book about a romantic composer's circle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I've a' said in a non-rhotic accent sounds like IVOR; 'short' only describes the book, a novella, which 'unfinished' trims to NOVELL; 'of the' links.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivor Novello was a popular British composer of romantic songs and musicals in the early twentieth century.

clue.text: The bloke's embracing crossword setters' voluptuous women

indicators.note: embracing means holding inside, so one word wraps around the other

parts.note: the bloke's means belonging to him, his
setters speak of themselves collectively, so their possession is 'our'

explanation.surface: A man hugs the setters' alluring women.
explanation.definitionFit: Houris are beautiful maidens of the Islamic paradise, used loosely for alluring women.

clue.text: Sound of involuntary personal outburst in dispute you might hear

indicators.note: you might hear means the phrase is taken as spoken, not as spelt

parts.note: a matter in dispute is at issue

explanation.surface: During an argument someone hears an uncontrolled personal outburst.
explanation.walkthrough: AT ISSUE spoken aloud sounds like a sneeze.
explanation.definitionFit: Atishoo is the British rendering of a sneeze, an outburst the body makes on its own.

clue.text: Dearest gin used to seduce one into implicating oneself

definitions.text: used to seduce one into implicating oneself

parts.note: honey is an endearment like dearest
a gin is a snare or trap

explanation.surface: A beloved's gin is used to lure a person into self-incrimination.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gin' is not the drink but an old word for a snare.
explanation.definitionFit: A honeytrap is a scheme using seduction to lure someone into compromising or incriminating themselves.

clue.text: Go make good!

definitions.meaning: to ... to a place is to go there
to fix or mend something damaged

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to betake oneself somewhere and to mend, two separate senses.

clue.text: Into Soul? Perhaps this is what you're after

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the letters could be arranged otherwise

explanation.surface: A puzzler wonders whether a soul search is what they really want.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' rearranges INTO SOUL; the definition speaks to the solver.
explanation.definitionFit: A solver is after the correct answer to the clue, which is a solution.

clue.text: Out of the running, yeti grabs two points — a nightmare scenario

indicators.note: out signals the letters that follow are thrown into disorder

parts.note: E is the compass point east, taken twice

explanation.surface: A yeti, no longer a contender, seizes two points in a terrible turn of events.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out' is the indicator, so 'of' is fodder: OF THE RUNNING plus YETI plus EE, rearranged; 'grabs' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: Orwell's novel depicts a totalitarian dystopia, a by-word for a nightmarish future.

clue.text: Her squeak at random, caused by passing plates?

indicators.note: at random means in no set order, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A woman squeaks randomly as dishes go past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at' is part of the fodder; 'random' alone is the indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: Earthquakes result from tectonic plates of the Earth's crust sliding past each other.

clue.text: "Southern beer's rubbish" left out of commercial campaign!

parts.note: ales are beers, the plural standing in for beer's

indicators.note: out of means the letter is removed from the word

parts.note: drivel is nonsense or rubbish

explanation.surface: Someone protests that criticism of southern beer was omitted from an advert.
explanation.definitionFit: A sales drive is a concerted effort to boost a company's sales, a commercial campaign.

clue.text: Cartesian solecism motivated by religious hatred

indicators.note: a solecism is an error, so the word is written incorrectly

explanation.surface: A grammatical blunder in Descartes's philosophy sparks bigotry.
explanation.definitionFit: Sectarian describes bigotry arising from divisions between religious sects.

clue.text: See 11
Prison with club, hospital and something for garden visitors to wallow in

definitions.text: something for garden visitors to wallow in

parts.note: bird is British slang for a prison sentence or prison
a bat is a club for striking a ball

explanation.surface: A jail, a club and a hospital listed with a garden fixture.
explanation.definitionFit: A birdbath is a shallow basin placed in gardens for wild birds to bathe in.

clue.text: Choke reindeer, one making an entertaining clatter

parts.note: to choke a pipe is to clog it
Dancer is one of Santa's reindeer

explanation.surface: A reindeer chokes, making an amusing racket.
explanation.definitionFit: A clog dancer performs in wooden shoes, rapping out rhythms as entertainment.

clue.text: Asses reason (wrongly) it's good to be inside

indicators.note: to be inside means the letter goes within the jumbled word
wrongly means the letters of reason are set out incorrectly

explanation.surface: Donkeys argue incorrectly that staying indoors is good.
explanation.definitionFit: Onagers are wild asses of Asia, so a plural synonym.

clue.text: Recording the score of "King Hal" in reverse order aboard vessel

indicators.note: aboard means placed inside, so the words go inside the container

parts.note: a cup is a drinking vessel

indicators.note: in reverse order means the two words of the quoted name are swapped

explanation.surface: Someone notes the music of a royal work, played backwards on board a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'King Hal' becomes HAL KING; 'vessel' looks like a ship but is a cup.
explanation.definitionFit: Chalking up means scoring or recording points, as on a scoreboard in a pub game.

clue.text: As Jupiter is, gigantically, so usage determined

indicators.note: determined is taken as freshly settled, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Jupiter's vast size is settled by common usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Jupiter is a gas giant, a huge planet made mainly of gas.

clue.text: Chap is hot from the wall erector

indicators.note: from means the letter is taken away from the name

parts.note: the emperor Hadrian built a wall across northern England
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A man is said to be hot, coming from the builder of a wall.
explanation.definitionFit: Adrian is a man's name, and crosswords often define names as a chap.

clue.text: Novel manual evidence of a serious neglect of household vacuuming?

definitions.text: manual evidence of a serious neglect of household vacuuming?
definitions.meaning: a scoop of grime in the hand, proof the hoovering has not been done

explanation.definitionFit: The title is Waugh's novel and, literally, a handful of grime collected from an unswept house.

clue.text: See 1
The best in cold desserts — break open "the hard stuff" with them

definitions.text: break open "the hard stuff" with them

indicators.note: in means one word is placed within the other

parts.note: ices are frozen desserts
the pick of something is its best

explanation.surface: The finest frozen puddings are shattered, ice being the hard stuff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the hard stuff' suggests strong drink but means ice.
explanation.definitionFit: Ice picks are pointed tools used to chip blocks of ice apart.

clue.text: Was an informer about to steal hemless skirt?

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one word wraps the other

parts.note: an informer sings to the police, so sang

indicators.note: a hem is at the bottom, so the final letter is cut off

parts.note: to steal is to rob

explanation.surface: An informer was about to steal a skirt with no hem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' only links; 'hemless' trims the bottom, i.e. the final letter, as a hem is a skirt's lower edge.
explanation.definitionFit: A sarong is a length of cloth wrapped round the waist as a skirt.

clue.text: Absence of evil: an added indication of female's curiosity

parts.note: having no evil is no sin
the suffix -ess, added to a noun as in lioness, marks a female

explanation.surface: Purity plus a feminine touch is put down to a woman's inquisitiveness.
explanation.walkthrough: 's' links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Nosiness is prying inquisitiveness about others' affairs, a form of curiosity.

clue.text: Hythe's isolated housing position advanced

indicators.note: housing means the letters are contained within the words

explanation.surface: An isolated spot in Hythe, a Kent coastal town, hides a forward position.
explanation.walkthrough: Hythe is a town on the Kent coast.
explanation.definitionFit: A thesis is a proposition put forward in an argument, a position advanced.
